title: Circle discrepancy bounds and Beck's remaining log-gap questions

problemStatement.formal: For every infinite point sequence A in R^2, circleDiscrepancy_A(r) is unbounded and admits a universal sqrt(r) lower bound; some A has O(sqrt(r log r)) discrepancy.
problemStatement.plain: Erdos 989 asks whether circle discrepancy is unbounded and how fast it must grow. The Lean file defines circle discrepancy, packages Beck's lower and upper bounds as axioms, proves unboundedness from the lower bound, and records open questions about the logarithmic gap, explicit constructions, and higher dimensions.
whyMatters: Places the solved Erdos question inside geometric discrepancy theory.
Identifies the remaining gap between Beck's universal lower bound and probabilistic upper bound.

proven: `Circle.disk`, `PointSequence`, `countInCircle`, `localDiscrepancy`, and `circleDiscrepancy` define the geometric discrepancy setup.
`discrepancy_unbounded` derives unboundedness for every sequence from Beck's lower bound.
`erdos_989_solved` and `erdos_989_answers_both_questions` package the solved status of the original questions.
`openQuestion_logarithmic_gap`, `openQuestion_explicit_construction`, and `openQuestion_higher_dimensions` record the remaining discrepancy-theory directions.
open: `beck_lower_bound` and `beck_upper_bound` are axioms; Fourier-analytic and probabilistic proofs are not formalized.
The logarithmic gap between sqrt(r) and sqrt(r log r) remains a mathematical open problem.
Explicit optimal constructions and higher-dimensional log factors remain open directions.
knownResults.goal: Use the current definitions to stage smaller discrepancy-theory lemmas before attempting Beck's axiomatized lower and upper bounds.
